Extending rdantic: new_type()

Source: vignettes/extending-rdantic.Rmd
extending-rdantic.Rmd
library(rdantic)
#> 
#> Attaching package: 'rdantic'
#> The following object is masked from 'package:graphics':
#> 
#>     frame
#> The following object is masked from 'package:base':
#> 
#>     date

Most custom rules fit inside type_from() (vignette("types-in-depth")): a predicate, an optional coercion, and rdantic looks after the problem format for you. This vignette covers new_type(), the lower-level constructor that everything else in the package – int, list_of(), struct(), fn() – is itself built from, for when a type needs full control over its validation and its JSON Schema fragment.

What a type actually is

A type is a closure that validates a value, carrying a spec attribute describing it (name, validate, schema, and whatever else the constructor stored). Calling a type runs validate(); printing it, or asking schema() for its JSON Schema, reads the rest of the spec. new_type() is how that closure gets built:

even <- new_type(
  "even",
  validate = function(x, path) {
    if (is.numeric(x) && all(x %% 2 == 0)) x else rdantic:::.bad(path, "even", type_of(x))
  },
  schema = function() list(type = "integer", multipleOf = 2)
)
even
#> <type> even
even(c(2, 4))
#> [1] 2 4
even(3)
#> Error:
#> ! 1 validation problem in even
#>   <value>  expected even, got num[1]

validate receives the value and the path at which it appears (so an error nested inside a struct or a list reports the right location) and returns either the – possibly coerced – value, or a problem record built by rdantic’s internal helpers. type_of() (exported, used above) renders a value the way rdantic names types in its own error messages, so a custom type’s errors read the same as a built-in one’s.

schema(even)
#> $type
#> [1] "integer"
#> 
#> $multipleOf
#> [1] 2

When to reach for this vs. type_from()

Need Use
A predicate, maybe a coercion, default JSON Schema shape type_from()
Full control over the problem message, or a custom JSON Schema fragment new_type()
A restricted set of exact values one_of()
A record with named fields struct()

In practice new_type() is rarely needed directly – it exists so the rest of rdantic can be implemented in terms of it, and remains available for the rare case a project’s own domain type needs the same level of control.
